topic: Law change: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026 - honest discount prices (lowest price in last 30 days), country of origin, labelled sponsored listings, dark pattern self-audits, faster grievance handling; in force from 1 January 2027

slides.title: New rules for **shopping apps**
slides.subtitle: The Centre has tightened the e-commerce rules to protect **online buyers**. They apply from **1 January 2027**.
slides.cite: **Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026** · Ministry of Consumer Affairs

slides.label: Discounts
slides.title: No more **fake** "sale" prices
bullets: When a platform announces a discount, it must show the new price **and the prior price**.
The prior price means the **lowest price** offered in the **30 days** before the sale. So you can see how big the cut really is.
slides.note: **Law fact:** In 2025, about **29%** of complaints to the National Consumer Helpline were about e-commerce.

slides.label: Know what you buy
slides.title: More details **before** you pay
bullets: Product pages must show details like **best-before date**, return and refund terms, warranty, delivery and payment options.
For imported goods, the **country of origin** and importer details must be shown.
Paid ads in search results must be clearly marked as **sponsored**.

slides.label: Tricks and complaints
slides.title: Fair design, **faster** answers
bullets: Platforms must follow the **dark patterns** guidelines, audit themselves every year, and display a compliance certificate.
Complaints must be **acknowledged within 48 hours** and resolved within **one month**. You get a copy of your recorded complaint.
No bundled fees for unrelated services, except loyalty or membership plans.

slides.label: Keep in mind
slides.title: Not in force **yet**
bullets: These changes apply from **1 January 2027**. Until then, the existing 2020 e-commerce rules continue.
Keep screenshots of prices and offers when you shop. They help if you need to complain.
This post is for information only, not legal advice.

caption:
That "70% off" tag on your shopping app may soon have to tell the truth 🛒⚖️

The Centre has notified the Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026. They will apply from 1 January 2027. The biggest change for buyers: when a platform shows a discount, it must also show the prior price, which means the lowest price offered in the 30 days before the sale. So you can check how real the discount is.

Product pages will also need to show details like best-before dates, return and refund terms, warranty, delivery and payment options. Imported goods must show the country of origin and importer details. Paid placements in search results must be clearly marked as sponsored, and platforms cannot manipulate search results to mislead you.

Platforms must follow the dark patterns guidelines, do a yearly self-audit and display a compliance certificate. Complaints must be acknowledged within 48 hours and resolved within one month, and you get a copy of your recorded complaint. Marketplaces also cannot charge bundled fees for unrelated services, except loyalty or membership plans. Until 1 January 2027, the existing 2020 rules continue.

Law: Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) (Amendment) Rules, 2026, Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
